text:
Separating punishment from its justification matters because it lets us define punishment as a value-neutral practice—deliberately imposing hardship for an offense—without building in a contested rationale like retribution or deterrence. Conflating them makes one justification seem essential to punishment itself, obscuring alternatives and biasing debates about when punishment is permissible. So the key point is that any definition of punishment should be value-neutral.
